problem: Sales teams juggle about ten tools and cold email suffers low open and reply rates and deliverability problems; rift combined email, dialer, scheduler and lead routing.
business_model: B2B SaaS sales platform with demo led onboarding
product_category: Sales automation and lead routing, started as cold email deliverability

founders.name: Fil Twarowski
founders.background_notes: First business hire at Pulley (YC page).

founders.name: Edvard Eriksson
founders.background_notes: Product and growth lead; the launch post and Sequoia call him Eddie. Worked in growth at Samsara and Pulley (YC page).

exit.reason: YC lists as inactive; rift.com now redirects to a domain broker page; no public shutdown or acquisition notice found

technical_complexity.rationale: Email infrastructure, deliverability management, scheduling and routing combined in one product; standard SaaS engineering with deliverability as a hard operational problem.

defensibility.rationale: Many point tools covered each feature; an all in one suite relies on execution and integrations.

market_need_then: The launch post cites cold email open rates under 50 percent, reply rates near 1 percent and bounce rates near 5 percent; Sequoia cites teams using ten different tools.

branding.domain_note: Used getrift.com for the app and demo, rift.com listed on YC; rift.com now redirects to a domain broker page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, benefit focused (close more deals without landing in spam)

brand_strength.rationale: A Sequoia partnership post gave some visibility but the name collides with several other companies called Rift and no community evidence found.

outcome_analysis: rift raised a Sequoia led seed in July 2024 after launching in the W23 batch with a cold email deliverability pitch and later a broader sales platform and lead routing product. YC lists it inactive and rift.com no longer hosts the product, but no source explains why, so the outcome and cause are not public.
notes: The Sequoia post (dated July 24 2024) states the lead but not the amount; $5M comes from FinSMEs and FounderLodge snippets (FinSMes page returned 403 when fetched); Y Combinator and Soma Capital come from a search summary of those outlets. Search result summaries conflicted on Active versus Inactive; the YC page fetched now says Inactive. A Signalbase item claiming $96M for a company named rift was not tied to this company and is ignored. Seedtable lists a Nov 2025 seed under rift-2 that was not verified as this company. The YC page descriptions differ (lead routing on the company page, cold email deliverability in the launch post); no dated pivot is sourced. Competitors left empty: only undated vendor pages (LeanData, Chili Piper, Instantly) found.
